unknowns: Which RT_STRING numbering the original game addresses strings with: this engine numbers a row (block - 1) * 16 + index (Documented) and the documented Win32 rule for the same leaf is one block apart, uniformly. Resolving task #374; it gates every id this command reports and the retail test's id 3480 is the engine's own numbering, not a verified original id.

Whether a localized installation keeps langui.dll's block ids, language 1033 and code page 0: only one English installation was surveyed, so F12-D AC04 (a localized installation preserves stable ids while changing display text) stays open for the F12-D stage and for the M02-A..M24-A title confirmations that follow.
Whether the game reaches these strings through the Win32 resource API, through the project's own RESOURCE.H, or through both: recorded on the pe.resources dialect row, not measured.

The lead left for #374 and not measured here: the original's own ASSETS/SCRIPTS/RESOURCE.H ('Used by LangUI.rc') defines IDS_MISSIONAREA 1220 and langui.dll's engine-numbered id 1220 is a region string; the block name of that leaf decides the numbering and was not read.

review.identity: Regenerated by the reviewer bunny-2 (Space Bunny Free, a different agent instance with fresh context) on the rebased review tree, after it added two acceptance tests and corrected one doc comment; the implementer of the routing change was bunny-alpha-1. The reviewer re-ran every command in this report. The report is still not independent original-reference evidence: no agent ran the original game, so per AGENTS.md a merge awards `checked` at most.
review.method: Generated by private/evidence/F12-D.langui/harness.py on candidate tree 76f5abbd7bbf9c52061a4ecec6d2f0075a1064de from real runs, not written by hand: the task selection (`cargo test --workspace --locked -- accept_f12_d_ --include-ignored`) and then each discovered acceptance test again with `--exact --include-ignored` (both in cargo-test.log), plus one `cs-inspect config` report per surveyed PE image with no `--container` override and one `cs-inspect inventory` run whose `fingerprints` supply install_sha256 and content_sha256. The capabilities are `synthetic` (the six fixture-image tests) and `retail` (the one test that reads $CS_GAME_DIR, the three config reports and the inventory). `retail` means read access to the installation files; the original executable was not run, so the claim is `implemented` and no behaviour claim is made. The report keeps its `unknowns` non-empty, so `tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass` rejects it with 'Unresolved issues' by design (the T351 precedent): dropping them to make the flag pass would hide that F12-D's AC04 and #374 are open. Only hashes and paths are committed; the artifacts, which contain original strings, stay in private/. The report is committed after this run, so the committed candidate_tree is the tree of its parent commit and the only later delta is this report's own copy under docs/findings/evidence/.
